title: How an owned process tree is stopped: ask first, kill after a declared grace, and say who did it
description: An owned command that is cancelled, times out or exceeds a ceiling gets SIGTERM for its whole owned tree (POSIX groups and descendants, found before ancestry is lost). A caller forwarding an interrupt can send SIGINT first. The tree gets `graceMilliseconds` to end by itself (looked at every `pollMilliseconds`), and only what is still alive afterwards gets SIGKILL. Windows has no signal to ask with and keeps `taskkill /T /F`. Every recorded signal names the victim, the signal, the killing process, the command and the reason in English and German, and the creation time of victim and sender. A signal goes only to a process whose creation time still matches the snapshot it was found in (a reused pid is never signalled), and a process group is signalled as a group only while every process in it belongs to the owned tree; an orphan that kept the group of a dead root is part of the tree.
